newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kuwait term naphtha premium set at $18 - traders.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait term naphtha premium set at $18 - traders.

text.p: Asian buyers of Kuwaiti term naphtha cargoes have accepted Kuwait Petroleum Corp's (KPC) offer price of $18 per tonne over the mean of Middle Eastern quotes for annual supply contracts starting in August, traders said on Wednesday.
The new price compared with a $7.90 premium set for the one-year term contracts that started in August 1996, and a $13.50 premium for the other term year that began in March 1997.

The term lifters -- trading houses, oil firms and petrochemical manufacturers from Japan and South Korea -- are expected to import about 2.5 million to three million tonnes of naphtha cargoes during the new term year, traders said.

Prior to the KPC term talks that started last week in London, Saudi Arabia set the term price for its Jubail naphtha, which is similar in quality to KPC material, at $15.00 per tonne over the Aramco formula for the second half of 1997.
The new price for Jubail cargoes can roughly be translated into $21.00 over the mean of Middle Eastern quotes, traders said.
